plan.english: Mother, why are you weeping? Your father is dead. Young men of the other lineage killed him at the feast. Ill-Minded struck him with a knife and fled in the night. title: The feud of the two houses

plan.english: Two houses stood by the river. In the one house dwelt Of-Good-Fame; in the other dwelt Man-Minded. Of-Good-Fame stole a horse from Man-Minded and killed him. The orphan of Man-Minded grew up and killed Of-Good-Fame with a spear. Then the offspring of Of-Good-Fame struck him down on the path. The grandsons fought at the ford, and they fell. No one gave a price, and no one took one. The women became widows and grew old. Now grass grows on their hearths.

clauses.english: Two houses stood by the river.

Of-Good-Fame stole a horse from Man-Minded and killed him.

No one gave a price, and no one took one.
The women became widows and grew old.

plan.english: A widow nourished her boy. In the nights she said to him: Ill-Minded killed your father. He still lives. The boy grew strong. She gave him the dead man's spear. He went to the dwelling of Ill-Minded and killed him at his hearth. Then the lineage of Ill-Minded came in the night and burned her house. The widow and the boy died in the fire. So vengeance devoured two houses.

plan.english: A herdsman swore an oath by Sky. He said: I will pay the blood-price at harvest. Harvest came, and he did not pay. By night he fled with his herd. At the ford the water rose, and the river took him and the herd. The Sun had seen his lie. His orphans did not find his body. No earth covered him. Whoever breaks an oath, the gods do not forget him. The old men say that.

title: The widow who drove back the cattle

plan.english: The enemy's kin led a hundred calves to the widow. She did not take them. She drove them back to the slayer's door. For seven years they led the calves to her, and she drove them back. Her orphan grew up. Then she gave him a knife and said: Now bring me the price. He brought blood; he did not bring cattle. The widow smiled, and that night she slept.

title: The elder who judged his son

plan.english: Of-True-Fame, the elder's son, struck down a guest at the feast. The guest's lineage came to the assembly and asked for a payment. The elder said to Of-True-Fame: Pay the price of the guest. Of-True-Fame said: I will not pay. Then the elder decided: Go away from our village. You are not my son. The young man went away, and the old man gave the payment with his own cattle. There was peace between the two houses. But the old man's tears poured out at the door.

plan.english: Whoever kills a free man, let him give a hundred cows to the kin of the dead man. Whoever kills a woman, let him also give a hundred cows. Whoever strikes down a child, let him pay twice. If he does not give, let the lineage of the dead take his blood. If they take the price, let no one shed blood.

Whoever strikes down a child, let him pay twice.
If he does not give, let the lineage of the dead take his blood.
If they take the price, let no one shed blood.

plan.english: If a man sheds a kinsman's blood at a feast, let no one seat him at his hearth. Let him not drink mead with the men. Let no one speak his name. If anyone kills a guest under a roof, let the master of the house pay the guest's price, because he guards him. A guest is dear to the gods.

clauses.english: If a man sheds a kinsman's blood at a feast, let no one seat him at his hearth.
Let him not drink mead with the men.
Let no one speak his name.
If anyone kills a guest under a roof, let the master of the house pay the guest's price, because he guards him.
A guest is dear to the gods.

plan.english: Hear, kin of the slayer and kin of the dead man! I have heard the two houses. The slayer struck him with a spear. So I decide: Let him give a hundred cows and ten horses. Let the kin of the dead man take them, and let them not shed blood. Let both houses swear it by Perkʷunos. Whoever breaks this pledge, let the gods punish him.

clauses.english: Hear, kin of the slayer and kin of the dead man!
I have heard the two houses.
The slayer struck him with a spear.
So I decide:
Let him give a hundred cows and ten horses.
Let the kin of the dead man take them, and let them not shed blood.
Let both houses swear it by Perkʷunos.
Whoever breaks this pledge, let the gods punish him.

plan.english: Whoever swears by Sky and lies, let him pay twice. May no one trust that man. If a man promised a price and did not give it, let his kin give it. The Sun sees the oaths.

clauses.english: Whoever swears by Sky and lies, let him pay twice.
May no one trust that man.
If a man promised a price and did not give it, let his kin give it.
The Sun sees the oaths.

title: Of the widow and the son

plan.english: If a dead man leaves a small orphan, let the widow hold the payment. When he has grown up, let him decide. If the widow does not take the price, let no one threaten her. Grief is not a trade.

clauses.english: If a dead man leaves a small orphan, let the widow hold the payment.
When he has grown up, let him decide.
If the widow does not take the price, let no one threaten her.
Grief is not a trade.

plan.english: Husband, beloved, where are you? You went to the great feast at evening. Then they carried you back at night. Your blood lies on my hands. Your hearth has grown cold, and your orphans are small. I will not take their cattle. Weep, women of the villages!

clauses.english: Husband, beloved, where are you?
You went to the great feast at evening.
Then they carried you back at night.
Your blood lies on my hands.
Your hearth has grown cold, and your orphans are small.
I will not take their cattle.
Weep, women of the villages!

plan.english: Son, bright one, you lie in the earth. Who now will drive your herd? My daughter-in-law weeps at the door. Then an old vengeance devoured you. Your blood lies on the stone. I will not forget you; may the gods give you rest.

clauses.english: Son, bright one, you lie in the earth.
Who now will drive your herd?
My daughter-in-law weeps at the door.
Then an old vengeance devoured you.
Your blood lies on the stone.
I will not forget you; may the gods give you rest.

plan.english: My father fell, and my sons fell. My dear grandsons fell. I sit alone at the hearth. So vengeance devoured my lineage. Who will lay me in the earth? Sky, why did you not see my grief?

clauses.english: My father fell, and my sons fell.
My dear grandsons fell.
I sit alone at the hearth.
So vengeance devoured my lineage.
Who will lay me in the earth?
Sky, why did you not see my grief?

plan.english: Dear brother, I will not forget you. They gave a hundred calves. The calves are fat, and you are dead. I will not eat their sweet flesh. In the nights I see your blood. May the gods remember you, brother.

clauses.english: Dear brother, I will not forget you.
They gave a hundred calves.
The calves are fat, and you are dead.
I will not eat their sweet flesh.
In the nights I see your blood.
May the gods remember you, brother.

plan.english: Now my brother has killed my husband's brother. For whom shall I, a wretched woman, weep? Now my mother-in-law hates me. My husband's sister is silent. My children hate my brother. Black night, take me now.

clauses.english: Now my brother has killed my husband's brother.
For whom shall I, a wretched woman, weep?
Now my mother-in-law hates me.
My husband's sister is silent.
My children hate my brother.
Black night, take me now.

title: Curse on the slayer of a husband

plan.english: Slayer of my husband, hear me! May your cows die in the field. May your young ones not grow up. May your hearth grow cold for all time. May sleep not come to you. May the dogs of the household and the birds eat you. May no kinsman lay you down.

clauses.english: Slayer of my husband, hear me!
May your cows die in the field.
May your young ones not grow up.
May your hearth grow cold for all time.
May sleep not come to you.
May the dogs of the household and the birds eat you.
May no kinsman lay you down.

plan.english: You made a vow by Sky, and you lied. May the bright Sun see you. And now may your oath break you. May your words be wind. May fire not warm you. May your kin not know your name.

clauses.english: You made a vow by Sky, and you lied.
May the bright Sun see you.
And now may your oath break you.
May your words be wind.
May fire not warm you.
May your kin not know your name.

plan.english: May the wolf find your sheep. And then may your fields dry up. May your mead become blood. May your swift horses flee from you. May the milk of your cows rot. May kin wish you evil things.

clauses.english: May the wolf find your sheep.
And then may your fields dry up.
May your mead become blood.
May your swift horses flee from you.
May the milk of your cows rot.
May kin wish you evil things.

plan.english: You struck me in the black night. May my blood follow you. May my sons hunt you. May your knife break in your hand. May your good fame perish. May your name be lost among mortals.

clauses.english: You struck me in the black night.
